clarifications.ref_id_rule: Caller input is limited to three Zod-validated fields — `runId` (`[A-Za-z0-9]{8,32}`), `caseId` (fixed §4 allowlist) and `refId` (lowercase UUID, supplied only for cases that address a record) — and only the validated `refId` fills the single `{id}` parameter of the fixed `/api/v1/users/{id}` route template, never a caller-supplied URL or path. All other method, path template, header and body values are fixed per case; arbitrary caller-supplied URL, path, method, header or body overrides are forbidden, so the endpoint is **not a proxy**.
clarifications.app_client_envelope: - **App-client:** `outcome` (`value` / `apiError` / `abort`); when `outcome` is `value`, `value` carries the harness-local Zod-validated native User object (properties per §4 expectations) and `apiError` is `null`; when `outcome` is `apiError`, `value` is `null` and `apiError.{status, code, message, details}` is present; a caller `signal` abort leaves `value` and `apiError` `null` (client timeouts are `apiError` code `TIMEOUT`, not aborts, per client source); `classification` per §5.5. The shared client returns schema-validated body only on success — success HTTP status and response headers are not observable through it — so wire fields stay `null` (`not-observable-via-client`); wire evidence keeps its own request IDs/records; the shared client is unmodified.
clarifications.body_cap_rule: - Retained bodies (`value`, wire `upstream.body`) are capped at 16 KiB with a `truncated` flag set when capped. Truncation is an envelope-retention boundary only — the client parses and schema-validates the complete response body in memory — but a truncated retained value is never evidence of a complete response: rows asserting full-body equality (T2), field-for-field persistence comparison (INT-PERS-01/02 checkpoints) or full validated/persisted state are recorded BLOCKED (assertion not established, never PASS) unless the retained body is untruncated. Synthetic data only.
clarifications.native_503_pin: > **Native 503 source pin (accepted `52b60a4`):** every native unavailable problem returns exactly `type` `/problems/unavailable`, `detail` `"service temporarily unavailable"`, integer `retryAfter` `1` and `title` "Service Unavailable", pinned by `docs/api.md` L148–163, `internal/adapter/inbound/httpapi/errors.go` L58–78 (`unavailableDetail`, `retryAfterSeconds`) and `testdata/unavailable.golden` L1–15, with Codex-recorded file hashes in `docs/testing/step-02-3/native-503-source-pin.json`. Source pin only: no runtime replay, no new product `retryAfter`/`Retry-After` convention (product units/range/header remain deferred to D-11/G-5).
clarifications.client_source_support: Source-supplied `src/lib/api/http-client.ts` confirms at static source level: `headers?: HeadersInit` is supported (merged via `new Headers(options.headers)`; the client authoritatively sets `Accept: application/json` always and `Content-Type: application/json` whenever a body is given); `init` accepts `cache: 'no-store'` (typed `Omit<RequestInit, 'method' | 'body' | 'headers' | 'signal'>` and spread first in `fetch`, so it cannot override method/body/headers/signal); error mapping is `404→NOT_FOUND`, `400/422→VALIDATION_ERROR`, otherwise `HTTP_ERROR` (consistent with T8/T10/T11a asserting `HTTP_ERROR` on 409/412/503), transport failure `NETWORK_ERROR` status 0, timeout `TIMEOUT`, 2xx schema failure `INVALID_RESPONSE`. This closes the source-level gap for the pinned file only; it is not a runtime or test result, and INT-ENV-07's Next caching/cross-root/binding/dynamicity items remain NOT_RUN.
clarifications.db_stop_evidence: Strict no-change variant of T11b is optional and permitted only with this recorded causal chain: (1) the failed PATCH is a single known-ID `PATCH` with current `If-Match`; the POST case (T11c) always stays OUTCOME_UNKNOWN; (2) Codex-recorded PostgreSQL stop command, exit code and UTC timestamp, followed by a verified stopped-state check (container status / no owned listener), with UTC strictly earlier than the PATCH envelope `startedAt`; (3) stopped state re-verified after the failed PATCH and before restart, so the failure window contains no running DB; (4) container ID and storage identity recorded before stop and equal after start; (5) the harness is the sole writer of the owned DB during the window; (6) after recovery, read-only GET of A (INT-PERS-04) shows the pre-outage checkpoint (`id`, `version`, timestamps, current name) and no committed change. The unchanged conclusion cites this chain and its request IDs, never the 503 alone. If this class is not executable at ARCH-FINAL, drop the strict variant and keep OUTCOME_UNKNOWN with read-only reconciliation only.
